summary: The note covers the post of Governor of Vatican City (Governatore dello Stato della Città del Vaticano). It states that Marchese Camillo Serafini held the post from the founding of the state in 1929 until his death in 1952. It also notes that no successor was appointed and that the post is not mentioned in the Fundamental Law of Vatican City State of 2000.
one_line: The Governor of Vatican City was a post held by Marchese Camillo Serafini from 1929 until 1952 and later left unfilled.
key_facts: The post of Governor of Vatican City was called Governatore dello Stato della Città del Vaticano in Italian.
Marchese Camillo Serafini held the post of Governor of Vatican City from the foundation of the state in 1929.
Marchese Camillo Serafini held the post of Governor of Vatican City until his death in 1952.
No successor to Marchese Camillo Serafini was appointed as Governor of Vatican City.
The post of Governor of Vatican City is not mentioned in the Fundamental Law of Vatican City State.
The Fundamental Law of Vatican City State was issued by Pope John Paul II on 26 November 2000.
The Fundamental Law of Vatican City State entered into force on 22 February 2001.
